turn_text: All right, very interesting. I guess I should correct myself, not actually in your district, but in Wisconsin.

So I guess this kind of raises the question here. A lot of people have been talking about kind of US economic interest with China, like our companies going to pull out of China, pull their manufacturing out of China, and bring it back to the United States. And people are kind of concerned that If too many American companies or other companies pull out of China, that's maybe caused some sort of economic collapse in China. Are you worried about that economic collapse and what kind of corner that might back China into?

I think the bigger risk is that there could be an economic collapse in China at any moment given their demographic issues, given their mismanagement of their economy, given the lingering effects of their zero COVID policy. So in my opinion, the longer we remain dependent on China, the longer we allow manufacturing to be concentrated in China, the more vulnerable we are to that shock. So it's actually wise economic as well as national security policy to seek to reduce our dependency over the long term. Now it's not going to happen overnight. I recognize that. And there's always going to be some economic relationship with China. You know, Wisconsin farmers sell a lot of soybeans to China, for example, but the quicker we reduce our dependency in key areas, I think the less vulnerable will be to economic shock because it does look like China's entering an economic downturn. And as I alluded to before, the demographic challenges, though most acute in the next decade are really, really daunting and something that I don't think Xi Jinping is prepared to deal with.

They actually have far more tools at their disposal than say the Soviet Union did for repression. They're trying to succeed where the Soviet Union failed. But over time, I think it it it points us to what is our our relative strength, which is that our system and the values it represents are better than the system, the sort of techno totalitarian system that the Chinese Communist Party is not only trying to perfect within the borders of China, but increasingly export around the world.
